en: Nativism - A policy of promoting the interests of native inhabitants against those of immigrants.
Neo-colonialism - The use of economic, political, and other pressures to control or influence other countries, especially former colonies.
New World Order - A shift or transformation in global political power.
Non-Aligned Movement - Countries not formally aligned with any major power bloc.
Non-tariff Barriers - Trade barriers that restrict imports or exports of goods or services through mechanisms other than the simple imposition of tariffs.
Nuclear Deterrence - The strategy of preventing an enemy from launching a nuclear attack by threatening nuclear retaliation.
Offshoring - Relocating a company's business process to another country.
Oil Glut - An excessive amount of oil supply leading to lower prices.
Oligarchy - A form of power structure where power rests with a small number of people.
OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) - An intergovernmental organization of 14 nations, founded to coordinate and unify the petroleum policies of its member countries.
Pax Americana - Peace in the Western world established by the dominant power of the United States.
Petrodollar - U.S. dollars earned by a country through the sale of its petroleum to another country.
Petty Corruption - Everyday corruption, usually involving small amounts of money.
Pivot to Asia - U.S. foreign policy strategy focusing more on the Asian continent.
Political Economy - The interplay of economics, law, and politics in the shaping of public policy.
Populism - A political approach that strives to appeal to ordinary people.
Post-industrial Economy - An economy that no longer relies on heavy industry.
Power Vacuum - A situation where there is no clear leader or dominant authority in a system or organization.
Protectionism - The theory or practice of shielding a country's domestic industries from foreign competition.
Quantitative Easing (QE) - A monetary policy used by central banks to stimulate the economy by buying government securities or other securities from the market.
Quantitative Tightening (QT) - The reverse of QE, where central banks contract the money supply.
Quantum Computing - A new paradigm in computing where calculations are carried out using quantum-mechanical phenomena.
Quantum Diplomacy - Diplomatic strategies around quantum computing and its implications.
Realpolitik - Politics based on practical and material factors rather than ideological notions or moralistic premises.
Rentier State - A country that derives all or a substantial portion of its revenue from foreign entities renting its resources.
Resource Curse - The phenomenon where countries with an abundance of natural resources tend to have less economic growth and worse development outcomes.
Rust Belt - Areas of the northern US that experienced industrial decline starting around 1980.
Shadow Banking - Credit intermediaries that are not subject to regulatory oversight.
Silk Road 2.0 - Refers to China's Belt and Road Initiative, aiming to improve regional cooperation and connectivity.
Sinophobia - The fear or dislike of China, its people, or its culture.
Smart Power - Combination of hard power and soft power strategies.
Soft Power - The ability to shape the preferences of others through appeal and attraction rather than coercion.
South-South Cooperation - Collaboration between developing countries in the political, economic, social, cultural, or technical domains.
Sovereign Debt Crisis - When a country is unable to pay back or service its national debt.
Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) - A type of international monetary resource in the International Monetary Fund that operates as a supplement to the existing reserves of member countries.
Special Economic Zones (SEZs) - Designated areas in a country that have economic regulations different from the rest of the country.
Stagflation - Persistent high inflation combined with high unemployment and stagnant demand.
Strategic Autonomy - The capacity of a state to make its own choices and decisions independently.
Supply Chain Disruptions - Interruptions to the process of producing and delivering products.
Taper Tantrum - Refers to the 2013 collective reactionary panic after the U.S. Federal Reserve signaled the end of post-crisis QE.
